title: Multi-signal synthesis autoscaler spec for Dedicated fleets with staged decision and safety curtains
creator: Anika Rao
description: Goal: Define and implement an autoscaling policy engine that synthesizes multiple signals (throughput, P99 latency, request queue depth, GPU occupancy, and per-tenant headroom credits) to drive safe, cost-aware scaling decisions for Redwood Dedicated fleets. The engine must balance fast micro-scaling for transient bursts with conservative macro-scaling for sustained demand, while enforcing safety curtains (min-reserve, surge quarantine, cooldown windows) and deterministic rollback behavior. This ticket covers the policy spec, simulation knobs, rollout plan, and telemetry requirements.
background_and_rationale: Current autoscalers use single-dominant signals (typically throughput or P95 latency) and either aggressive or overly conservative step sizes. We have observed: 1) short token bursts causing oscillation and cost spikes, 2) headroom starvation on tenants with KV-cache affinity, and 3) slow reaction to sustained load leading to P99 regressions. A multi-signal synthesis approach reduces false positives and allows us to shape scaling actions by confidence and impact bands. Safety curtains let us bound worst-case cost and preserve stability for critical tenants.
proposal_summary: 1) Signals: ingest per-tenant token throughput (tokens/s), request arrival rate (rps), P99 latency, queue depth, GPU occupancy (util%), and headroom credit balance. 2) Scoring: normalize signals into a 0..1 urgency score per signal, then compute a weighted composite urgency. 3) Decision pipeline: fast-path micro-scaler (sub-60s decisions, small steps) for transient bursts when composite urgency < 0.7 and queue_depth spikes; slow-path deliberative scaler (2-10m window) for sustained load when composite urgency >= 0.7 or headroom low. 4) Stepper: gradient-limited steps (max +20% per step) with quantized instance increments matching SKU granularity. 5) Safety curtains: min_reserve (keep baseline X instances per tenant), surge_quarantine (probation window for newly scaled-up instances where rollback is prioritized), global_cost_cap (hard limit) and cooldown (2m micro, 10m macro). 6) Fallbacks: on telemetry gaps or control plane errors, shrink-to-min-reserve and enable degraded routing to hosted fallback models.
detailed_spec_notes:
- Normalization: use rolling 3m baseline per-signal with robust stats (median + MAD) to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
- Weighting defaults: throughput 0.35, P99 0.30, queue_depth 0.15, GPU_occupancy 0.10, headroom_credit 0.10; weights are configurable per-tenant class.
- Composite urgency thresholds: low <0.4 (no action), 0.4-0.7 (micro-scale), >=0.7 (macro-scale).
- Gradient limiter: delta_instances = min(max_delta, ceil(requested_capacity / instance_capacity)). max_delta defaults to 20% of current fleet rounded up.
- Credit system: each tenant accrues headroom credits for under-utilization; credits can be spent to allow temporary overruns without triggering macro-scale for up to N tokens/minute. Credits decay exponentially with half-life configured at fleet-level.
- Surge quarantine: newly added instances enter a 5-minute probation where they cannot be immediately removed unless under a failure condition.
- Eviction policy: prefer removing instances added most recently, avoid evicting instances hosting pinned customer work or KV-affine caches for >t_cache_sec.
- Metrics to emit: scaling_decision{tenant,mode,delta}, composite_urgency{tenant}, per_signal_score{tenant,signal}, headroom_credit_balance{tenant}, safety_event{type,reason}.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives:
- PID controller: simpler but more prone to oscillation with quantized instance sizes.
- ML-based demand predictor: potentially better forecasters but increases complexity and latency of decisions and requires additional training data.
- Pure throughput target: reacts quickly but ignores tail latency and cache affinity, leading to correctness issues for latency-sensitive tenants.
We choose a deterministic synthesis + credit system to provide transparency for SRE and tenant billing teams.
acceptance_criteria: Canary cluster runs for 72h without >1% P99 regressions under synthetic burst tests
Simulated workload runner: <3% cost increase vs previous baseline for same SLA when bursts are transient
No scaling oscillation (defined as >3 scale-up/scale-down cycles within 10 minutes) during chaos-net partition tests
Telemetry: composite_urgency and per_signal_score emitted at 10s granularity and visible in Console dashboard
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (spec + simulator): implement scoring + stepper and a deterministic simulator to run historical qps traces (owner: Diego)
Phase 2 (canary): wire into canary Dedicated fleet with conservative weights and small max_delta, 72h observation window (owner: SRE)
Phase 3 (gradual rollout): tenant-class rollout with opt-in for high-risk customers; expose weighting knobs in Console (owner: Product/Console)
Instrumentation: add tracing spans for decision path and record raw input signals for model explainability
Backward-compat: support legacy throughput-only mode via feature flag for rapid rollback
testing_and_simulation_plan:
- Build a synthetic workload harness covering: short bursts (1-30s), medium surges (2-10m), and steady ramp (30m+).
- Run A/B sims comparing current autoscaler vs multi-signal synthesizer across 100 historical tenant traces.
- Chaos tests: induce delayed telemetry, control-plane rate limits, and host preemption to validate safe fallback behavior.
- KPI checks: cost per effective token, P99 latency tail, number of scale cycles/pod-hour.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dev cluster smoke tests, 2) Canary on 2 Dedicated pools with low-impact tenants for 7 days, 3) Open to 10% of tenant volume with monitoring alerts, 4) Full fleet after 1 week meeting acceptance criteria. Contingency: rollback to throughput-only flag and drain newly added instances through surge_quarantine policy.
dashboards_and_alerts: Alert: sustained composite_urgency >= 0.75 for >5m triggers paging
Alert: >3 scale cycles in 10m triggers SRE runbook
